l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The preface, spoken by Yasumaro, explains the origins of Heaven and Earth, the succession of rulers, and the history of the empire up to the reign at Woharida. It recounts how the Heavenly Sovereign who governed the Eight Great Islands ascended at the Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka and ordered the correction and compilation of the imperial traditions. Hiyeda no Are memorized the genealogies and ancient words, and Yasumaro later recorded them under the Empress’s command. Yasumaro presents the resulting three volumes, with the First Volume covering the age from the Deity Master-of-the-August-Centre-of-Heaven to Prince-Wave-Limit-Brave-Cormorant-Thatch-Meeting-Incompletely.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The Kojiki is presented as a record compiled from the genealogies of the emperors and the ancient words preserved by various families. It consists of Three Volumes, beginning with the separation of Heaven and Earth and concluding with the august reign at Woharida.

l: Yasumaro, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: Yasumaro records the ancient words learned by heart by Hiyeda no Are, following the Imperial Decree. He explains the combined use of phonetic and ideographic writing and reverently presents Three Volumes.

l: the Empire, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The Empire is described as being pacified, purified, enlarged, and ruled through the succession of Heavenly Sovereigns. Its origins and history are recorded so that the great basis of the country and the foundation of the monarchy may be transmitted to later ages.

l: Heavenly Sovereign who governed the Eight Great Islands, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The Heavenly Sovereign governed the Eight Great Islands from the Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka. He ascended to the Heavenly seat, established divine reason and good customs, and ordered the imperial chronicles and ancient words to be corrected and recorded.

l: Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka was the place from which the Heavenly Sovereign governed the Eight Great Islands. It was also the place where he ascended to the Heavenly seat.

l: chronicles of the emperors, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The chronicles of the emperors were said to deviate from exact truth and to contain empty falsehoods. The Heavenly Sovereign ordered them to be selected, examined, corrected, and recorded for later ages.

l: original words in the possession of the various families, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The original words in the possession of the various families were reported to differ from exact truth and to be enlarged by falsehoods. They were to be examined, with falsehoods erased and the truth determined.

l: Hiyeda no Are, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: Hiyeda no Are was a retainer whose intelligence enabled him to repeat what he saw and remember what he heard. He was commanded to memorize the genealogies of the emperors and the words of former ages, which Yasumaro later recorded.

l: Empress, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The Empress is praised for obtaining Unity, illuminating the empire, nourishing the people, and extending her virtue and influence. She regretted errors in the old words and misstatements in the former chronicles, then commanded Yasumaro to record the words memorized by Hiyeda no Are.

l: Wa-do, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: In the fourth year of Wa-do, the Empress commanded Yasumaro to select and record the old words. The work was reverently presented on the 28th day of the first moon of the fifth year of Wa-dō.

l: Imperial Decree, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The Imperial Decree ordered the selection and recording of the chronicles of the emperors and the examination of the ancient words. Its purpose was to erase falsehoods, determine the truth, and transmit it to later ages.

l: First Volume, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The First Volume extends from the Deity Master-of-the-August-Centre-of-Heaven to His Augustness Prince-Wave-Limit-Brave-Cormorant-Thatch-Meeting-Incompletely. It contains the beginning of the records, including the separation of Heaven and Earth and the origins of the Deities and islands.

l: Heaven and Earth separation, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The separation of Heaven and Earth marks the beginning of the recorded account. It is associated with the commencement of creation and the emergence of the Three Deities.

l: imperial accession, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The imperial accession described in the preface occurs when the Heavenly Sovereign ascends to the Heavenly seat at the Great Palace of Kiyomihara at Asuka. He then obtains heavenly supremacy and annexes the Eight Wildernesses.

l: compilation of the records, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: The compilation of the records was undertaken to correct deviations and falsehoods in the imperial chronicles and ancient words. Hiyeda no Are supplied memorized material, and Yasumaro selected, arranged, explained, and recorded it in Three Volumes.

l: Court Noble Futo no Yasumaro, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods) / Preface.
s: Court Noble Futo no Yasumaro, an Officer of the Upper Division of the Fifth Rank and of the Fifth Order of Merit, reverently presented the completed Three Volumes on the 28th day of the first moon of the fifth year of Wa-dō.

s: The Beginning of Heaven and Earth concerns the birth of the first Deities. In the Plain of High Heaven, Master-of-the-August-Centre-of-Heaven, High-August-Producing-Wondrous Deity, and Divine-Producing-Wondrous-Deity were born alone and hid their persons. When the young Earth drifted about medusa-like, Pleasant-Reed-Shoot-Prince-Elder Deity and Heavenly-Eternally-Standing-Deity were born from something sprouting like a reed-shoot, and they likewise hid their persons. These five Deities are separate Heavenly Deities.

s: The Seven Divine Generations are described, beginning with the Earthly-Eternally-Standing-Deity and ending with the Female-Who-Invites. The Heavenly Deities command the Male-Who-Invites and Female-Who-Invites to make, consolidate, and give birth to the drifting land. Using a heavenly jewelled spear from the Floating Bridge of Heaven, they stir the brine until it becomes curdled, and the dripping brine forms the Island of Onogoro.
